import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Number of squares $\bmod n$

The number of squares modulo $n$.
This is the cardinality of the set $\{k^2 \bmod n \mid k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}\}$.

*References:*
- [A000224](https://oeis.org/A000224)
-/

namespace OeisA224

/-- The number of squares modulo $n$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 1
  else
    Finset.card ((Finset.range n).image (fun k : ℕ => k ^ 2 % n))

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

/--
$n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{a(n)(a(n)-1)}$ if and only if $n$ is an odd prime.
- Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    (n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2) ↔ n ^ 2 ≡ 1 [MOD a n * (a n - 1)] := by
  sorry

end OeisA224

findings.description: The attribution in the theorem's docstring says “Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017”. The cited OEIS entry dates this conjecture to April 13, 2025. This is a reference-date slip only; the mathematical statement is faithful.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A000224's %C comment reads: “Conjecture: n^2 == 1 (mod a(n)*(a(n)-1)) if and only if n is an odd prime. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Apr 13 2025.” Read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A000/A000224.seq. The April 27, 2025 snapshot contains the same attribution; the April 12, 2025 entry does not yet contain the conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring attribution to “Thomas Ordowski, Apr 13 2025”. No Lean statement change is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean extends the positive-indexed OEIS sequence to all natural numbers by setting a 0 = 1. OEIS specifies offset 1 and does not specify a zero-index value.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every n > 0, the definition is exactly the cardinality computed by the source's Maple program: distinct values of k² mod n for 0 ≤ k < n, including zero. The conjecture uses only n > 1, so this extension cannot change it; a_0 merely tests the chosen extension. The scratch file proves agreement with the cardinality formula on positive inputs and an equivalence showing that changing the sequence outside its positive domain leaves the conjecture unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly restricts n to n > 1, making the source congruence's positive-modulus domain explicit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 1, the distinct square residues 0 and 1 give a n ≥ 2, so a n * (a n - 1) is positive and natural subtraction agrees with integer subtraction. At n = 0 and n = 1, the chosen definition gives a n = 1 and hence modulus zero. Thus positive modulus is equivalent to n > 1. The scratch file proves this equivalence and equivalence of the guarded Lean statement to the positive-modulus formulation using 'odd prime'; it also verifies that n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2 means precisely an odd prime.
